question.problem: Let $X$ be the number obtained by a fair spinner with five sections labeled $-2,-1,1,2,3.$ What is $\text{SD}[X]?$
question.worked_solution:
The standard deviation of a random variable $X$ is defined as

$$
\text{SD}[X]=\sqrt{\text{Var}[X]},
$$

where the variance can be computed using the following formula:

$$
\text{Var}[X]=\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2}
$$

First, we need to compute the probability mass function $f(x).$ Here, there are $5$ possible outcomes ($-2,-1,1,2,3$) and each outcome has the same probability, so the probability mass function is as follows:

| $x$ | $-2$ | $-1$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $\frac{1}{5}$ | $\frac{1}{5}$ | $\frac{1}{5}$ | $\frac{1}{5}$ | $\frac{1}{5}$ |

Next, we compute $\text{E}[X].$ Summing up the products of each value of $X$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & =(-2)\cdot f(-2)+(-1)\cdot f(-1)+1\cdot f(1)+2\cdot f(2)+3\cdot f(3) \\  & =(-2)(\frac{1}{5})+(-1)(\frac{1}{5})+1(\frac{1}{5})+2(\frac{1}{5})+3(\frac{1}{5}) \\  & =\frac{3}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute $\text{E}[{X}^{2}].$ Summing up the products of each value of ${X}^{2}$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[{X}^{2}] & =(-2)^{2}\cdot f(-2)+(-1)^{2}\cdot f(-1)+{1}^{2}\cdot f(1)+{2}^{2}\cdot f(2)+{3}^{2}\cdot f(3) \\  & =4(\frac{1}{5})+1(\frac{1}{5})+1(\frac{1}{5})+4(\frac{1}{5})+9(\frac{1}{5}) \\  & =\frac{19}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the variance is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & =\text{E}[{X}^{2}]-\text{E}[X]^{2} \\  & =\frac{19}{5}-{(\frac{3}{5})}^{2} \\  & =\frac{19}{5}-\frac{9}{25} \\  & =\frac{95}{25}-\frac{9}{25} \\  & =\frac{86}{25}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{SD}[X] & =\sqrt{\text{Var}[X]} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{86}{25}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{86}}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
